literal: " Again Jie's forged-edict affair came to light; the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan and Jie was arrested and imprisoned.
idiomatic: " Jie's forged edict was exposed; at Wuyuan the emperor seized Jie and imprisoned him.

literal: Again Jie's forged-edict affair came to light; the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan and Jie was arrested and imprisoned.
idiomatic: Jie's forged edict was exposed; at Wuyuan the emperor seized Jie and imprisoned him.

literal: When the emperor set out on campaign, Jie had privately told his kin: "If the army goes out without success and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.
idiomatic: Before the march Jie had told his kin in private, "If the campaign fails and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.

literal: Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic texts and ask: "The Liu house is fated to rule—to succeed the state thereafter; do I in truth have a name and surname?
idiomatic: Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic books and ask, "The Liu house is fated to rule and succeed the state—do I truly have a name and surname among them?

literal: Song replied: "There is a surname but no name.
idiomatic: Song answered, "There is a surname but no name.

literal: Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book.
idiomatic: Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book.

literal: Jie, the Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred died.
idiomatic: Jie, Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred people died.

literal: Once Jie held a position of power, within and without all feared him—men watched him sidelong.
idiomatic: Once Jie held power, inside and outside the court all feared him—men watched him sidelong.

literal: When his household goods were inventoried, wealth exceeded tens of millions.
idiomatic: When his household was inventoried, his wealth ran to tens of millions.

literal: Taiwu, in retrospective anger, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.
idiomatic: Taiwu, looking back in fury, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.

literal: Qiu Dui, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Qiu Dui came from Dai.

literal: Fine in appearance.
idiomatic: He was fine in appearance.

literal: At first he entered service through loyal care.
idiomatic: At first he entered service through loyal care.

literal: When Mingyuan took the throne he attended at the ruler's side as remonstrator, and was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant at the Secretariat.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne he attended as remonstrator at the ruler's side and rose to regular attendant at the secretariat.

literal: When Taiwu supervised the state at court, Dui with Grand Commandant Mu Guan and the rest were right assistants.
idiomatic: When Taiwu oversaw affairs at court, Dui with Grand Commandant Mu Guan and others were right assistants.

literal: When he took the throne, Dui was granted the title Duke of Linhuai and made Grand Master of the Stud.
idiomatic: At his accession Dui was made Duke of Linhuai and grand master of the stud.

literal: He with Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing surveyed land in Guanzhong; Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin memorialized to retain Dui, and they combined armies to resist Helian Chang.
idiomatic: He with Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing surveyed land in Guanzhong; Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin asked to keep Dui, and they joined forces against Helian Chang.

literal: Jin advanced to attack Helian Ding; he left Dui to guard the baggage train.
idiomatic: Jin advanced against Helian Ding and left Dui to guard the baggage train.

literal: Jin was seized by Ding; hearing of it, Dui cast off his armor and fled to Chang'an.
idiomatic: Jin was taken by Ding; hearing of it, Dui threw off his armor and fled to Chang'an.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent Duke of Xiping An Yi to behead Dui.
idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and sent Duke of Xiping An Yi to execute Dui.

literal: E Qing, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: E Qing came from Dai.

literal: From youth he had military talent; he repeatedly won battle merit and was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: From youth he showed military talent, won repeated battle honors, and rose to attendant of the yellow gate.

literal: When Mingyuan toured the south and visited Ye, Qing was made General of the Central Army.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan toured south to Ye, Qing was made general of the central army.

literal: With Song general Zhou Ji and the rest he crossed the river, raided as far as Hulu, and for merit was granted the title Marquis of Xuchang.
idiomatic: With Song general Zhou Ji and others he crossed the river, raided to Hulu, and was made marquis of Xuchang for his merit.

literal: With Ji and the rest he then garrisoned Fangtou.
idiomatic: He then garrisoned Fangtou with Ji and the others.

literal: At the start of Taiwu's reign he returned to the capital and was advanced to Duke of Dongping.
idiomatic: At the opening of Taiwu's reign he returned to the capital and was raised to duke of Dongping.

literal: Later he followed in pacifying Tongwan and then with Xi Jin campaigned against Helian Chang, reaching Anding.
idiomatic: Later he joined the pacification of Tongwan and with Xi Jin campaigned against Helian Chang as far as Anding.

literal: When Chang's younger brother Ding fled west, Jin pursued him.
idiomatic: When Chang's brother Ding fled west, Jin pursued.

literal: Qing wished to go by water after him; Jin would not agree, and both were seized by Ding.
idiomatic: Qing wished to follow along the water; Jin refused, and both were taken by Ding.

literal: When Pingliang was taken, he was able to return.
idiomatic: When Pingliang fell he was able to return.

literal: Later he with Gu Bi and others campaigned east against Feng Hong; because he did not press the fight, Hong fled to Goryeo.
idiomatic: Later he campaigned east with Gu Bi against Feng Hong; because he would not press the attack, Hong fled to Goryeo.

literal: He was summoned in a caged cart, demoted to gate guard, and died at home.
idiomatic: He was hauled back in a prison cart, demoted to gate guard, and died at home.

literal: His son Yan was granted the title Duke of Nanping.
idiomatic: His son Yan was granted the title duke of Nanping.

literal: Yi Xu, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Yi Xu came from Dai.

literal: In youth he was brave and strong, could run with a galloping horse, was skilled at archery, and had strength to drag an ox walking backward.
idiomatic: As a youth he was brave and swift as a galloping horse, skilled at the bow, and strong enough to drag an ox walking backward.

literal: At the start of the Shengui era he was promoted to Gentleman.
idiomatic: At the start of the Shengui era he was promoted to gentleman.

literal: He was transferred to Inner Palace Guard of the Third Rank and granted the title Baron of Fenyang.
idiomatic: He was transferred to inner palace guard of the third rank and made baron of Fenyang.

literal: When Taiwu was about to campaign against Liangzhou, the deliberators all remonstrated that there was no grass or water; only Minister of Works Cui Hao urged the march.
idiomatic: When Taiwu was about to campaign against Liangzhou, every adviser said there was no grass or water; only Minister of Works Cui Hao urged the march.

literal: After the ministers had left, Xu said: "If Liangzhou had no grass or water, how could it be a state?
idiomatic: After the ministers withdrew, Xu said, "If Liangzhou lacked grass and water, how could it sustain a state?

literal: We should follow Hao's counsel.
idiomatic: We should follow Hao's advice.

literal: The emperor approved.
idiomatic: The emperor approved.

literal: When Liangzhou was taken, a great assembly was held at Guzang.
idiomatic: When Liangzhou fell, a great assembly was held at Guzang.

literal: The emperor told the ministers: "Master Cui's stratagems are more than enough—I am no longer surprised by them.
idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "Master Cui's stratagems are more than enough—I am no longer surprised by them.

literal: I am only surprised that Xu, a bow-and-horse man, sees as Hao does.
idiomatic: I am only surprised that Xu, a bow-and-horse man, sees as Hao does.

literal: He turned to Hao and said: "With intelligence such as this, Xu will in the end reach minister and duke rank.
idiomatic: He turned to Hao and said, "With intelligence such as this, Xu will in the end reach minister and duke rank.

literal: Hao said: "Why must one read books before one may be learned?
idiomatic: Hao said, "Why must one read books before one may be learned?

literal: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing also did not read books yet reached high office.
idiomatic: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing also did not read books yet reached high office.

literal: The emperor wished to make Xu Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoff him as Duke of a commandery.
idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Xu director of the masters of writing and enfeoff him as duke of a commandery.

literal: Xu said the director's duties were pressing and a commandery duke's rank too weighty, and declined;
idiomatic: Xu said the director's duties were pressing and a commandery duke's rank too weighty, and declined;

literal: the Central and Secretariat bureaus had many literary men, and he asked to serve in the second rank.
idiomatic: the central and secretariat bureaus had many literary men, and he asked to serve in the second rank.

literal: The emperor admired him and thereupon made him Director of the Secretariat and granted the title Duke of Henan.
idiomatic: The emperor admired him and made him director of the secretariat and duke of Henan.

literal: He was appointed Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He was appointed minister of works.

literal: Frugal and self-restrained, in government he set forth only the great outlines and was not harsh in petty matters.
idiomatic: Frugal and self-restrained, in government he set forth only the great outlines and was not harsh in petty matters.

literal: In the second year of Da'an he served as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
idiomatic: In the second year of Da'an he served as grand tutor to the crown prince.

literal: In the third year he with Minister of Works Lu Li and others jointly oversaw the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the third year he with Minister of Works Lu Li and others jointly oversaw the masters of writing.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Lan inherited the title and held office as Director of the Treasury.
idiomatic: His son Lan inherited the title and held office as director of the treasury.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: Lan died.

literal: His son Pensheng was valiant and bold, repeatedly won battle merit, and became a famed general.
idiomatic: His son Pensheng was valiant and bold, won repeated battle honors, and became a famed general.

literal: For merit he was granted the title Baron of Pingcheng.
idiomatic: For merit he was granted the title baron of Pingcheng.

literal: As commander of the western route he died in battle.
idiomatic: As commander of the western route he died in battle.

literal: He was posthumously made Inspector of Yong Province.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Yong province.

literal: Yi Gui, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Yi Gui came from Dai.

literal: His forebears for generations led the tribe.
idiomatic: His forebears for generations led the tribe.

literal: In Taiwu's time Gui's father Pizhi sent Gui to present tribute; the emperor detained him.
idiomatic: In Taiwu's time Gui's father Pizhi sent Gui to present tribute; the emperor detained him.

literal: Gui was skilled at mounted archery and could grapple fierce beasts with his hands.
idiomatic: Gui was skilled at mounted archery and could grapple fierce beasts with his hands.

literal: He married Taiwu's daughter Princess Shanggu, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and granted the title Duke of Xiping.
idiomatic: He married Taiwu's daughter Princess Shanggu, was made commandant of the horse guards, and granted the title duke of Xiping.

literal: He followed the southern campaign as commander-in-chief of the vanguard armies; his courage topped the three armies.
idiomatic: He followed the southern campaign as commander-in-chief of the vanguard; his courage topped the three armies.

literal: Later he was advanced to prince and also made commander of the western route.
idiomatic: Later he was advanced to prince and also made commander of the western route.

literal: He died at twenty-nine; posthumously he was made Duke of the Grand Commandant with the posthumous name Gong.
idiomatic: He died at twenty-nine; posthumously he was made duke of the grand commandant with the posthumous name Gong.

literal: His son Qiangui inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Qiangui inherited the title.

literal: His son Yuan, styled Yazhen, married Wencheng's daughter Princess Huaiyang, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and rose to Inspector of Western Yan Province.
idiomatic: His son Yuan, styled Yazhen, married Wencheng's daughter Princess Huaiyang, was made commandant of the horse guards, and rose to inspector of western Yan province.

literal: In the first year of Tianping he raised troops in support of Fan Zihe, was defeated in battle, and died.
idiomatic: In the first year of Tianping he raised troops in support of Fan Zihe, was defeated in battle, and died.

literal: Dou Daitian, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Dou Daitian came from Dai.

literal: In Mingyuan's time, for skill at mounted archery he was made Inner Fine Archer.
idiomatic: In Mingyuan's time, for skill at mounted archery he was made inner fine archer.

literal: In campaigning against Wulao an edict ordered Daitian to mount the tower and shoot the rebels; not an arrow missed.
idiomatic: In campaigning against Wulao an edict ordered Daitian to mount the tower and shoot the rebels; not an arrow missed.

literal: For merit he was promoted to Inner Palace Guard of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to inner palace guard of the third rank.

literal: In campaigning against Helian Chang he pursued the enemy in victory and entered their palace gate.
idiomatic: In campaigning against Helian Chang he pursued the enemy in victory and entered their palace gate.

literal: The gate was shut; Daitian climbed over the palace wall and came out.
idiomatic: The gate was shut; Daitian climbed over the palace wall and came out.

literal: Taiwu admired him and made him General of Martial Valor.
idiomatic: Taiwu admired him and made him general of martial valor.

literal: Later, in campaigning against Pingliang, he broke Helian Ding, recovered Xi Jin and the rest, and Ding's wife was granted to him.
idiomatic: Later, in campaigning against Pingliang, he broke Helian Ding, recovered Xi Jin and the rest, and Ding's wife was granted to him.

literal: An edict ordered Jin to advance on his knees and present wine to Daitian.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Jin to advance on his knees and present wine to Daitian.

literal: The edict told Jin: "He who preserved your life was Daitian's merit.
idiomatic: The edict told Jin, "He who preserved your life was Daitian's merit.

literal: For merit in campaigning against Helong he was enfeoffed Duke of Changgang.
idiomatic: For merit in campaigning against Helong he was enfeoffed duke of Changgang.

literal: He died as commander of Tongwan Garrison.
idiomatic: He died as commander of Tongwan garrison.

literal: Posthumously he was made Prince of Changgang with the posthumous name Gong.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made prince of Changgang with the posthumous name Gong.

literal: His son Zhouqiu inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Zhouqiu inherited the title.

literal: Che Yiluo, a man of Yanqi Hu stock.
idiomatic: Che Yiluo was of Yanqi Hu stock.

literal: For generations his line had been chieftain of the eastern-border tribes and had constantly paid tribute.
idiomatic: For generations his line had been chieftain of the eastern-border tribes and had constantly paid tribute.

literal: In the Yanhe era he was made General Who Pacifies the West and enfeoffed King of the Front Division.
idiomatic: In the Yanhe era he was made general who pacifies the west and enfeoffed king of the front division.

literal: Yiluo planned to return to court; Juqu Wuji cut the road, and Yiluo fought him repeatedly and broke him.
idiomatic: Yiluo planned to return to court; Juqu Wuji cut the road, and Yiluo fought him repeatedly and broke him.

literal: Wuji died.
idiomatic: Wuji died.

literal: Yiluo repeatedly sent envoys to win over Wuji's son Qianshou and the rest, and more than five hundred households were sent to the capital.
idiomatic: Yiluo repeatedly sent envoys to win over Wuji's son Qianshou and the rest, and more than five hundred households were sent to the capital.

literal: He also led more than two thousand of his tribesmen to campaign against Gaochang and broke seven cities of Yanqi's eastern pass.
idiomatic: He also led more than two thousand of his tribesmen against Gaochang and broke seven cities of Yanqi's eastern pass.

literal: In the second year of Zhengping, Yiluo came to court at the capital and was made Director of the Ministry of Justice; his general's rank and kingship were unchanged.
idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengping, Yiluo came to court and was made director of the ministry of justice; his general's rank and kingship were unchanged.

literal: He died; posthumous name King Kang; burial followed the precedent of Lu Luyuan.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous name King Kang; burial followed the precedent of Lu Luyuan.

literal: His son Xie inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Xie inherited the title.

literal: Che Lutou, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Che Lutou came from Dai.

literal: In youth, for loyal honesty he was chosen to serve the Eastern Palace and was made commander of the tent guard.
idiomatic: In youth, for loyal honesty he was chosen to serve the Eastern Palace and was made commander of the tent guard.

literal: At the end of the Tiansi era, when Mingyuan went abroad, Lutou followed and served with all his strength.
idiomatic: At the end of the Tiansi era, when Mingyuan went abroad, Lutou followed and served with all his strength.
